Times of Israel liveblog, 2 Nov 2026: Opposition parties to meet for coalition talks Tuesday, as leaders unite behind Eisenkot
The leaders of the four-party Zionist opposition bloc will hold their first joint meeting since last week's election tomorrow (Tuesday 3 Nov) at 11:30 a.m. at the Dan Accadia Hotel in Herzliya, the Yashar party says. Participants: Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar), Avigdor Liberman (Yisrael Beytenu), Yair Golan (Democrats), Naftali Bennett (B'Yachad), Yair Lapid (No. 2, B'Yachad). Purpose: to "discuss coordinating the bloc's next steps," per Yashar statement.
Liberman, Golan and Bennett have all said their parties will recommend Eisenkot as the next prime minister. Herzog expected to grant mandate to whoever receives most recommendations. Opposition considering using parliamentary majority to replace Likud's Amir Ohana as Knesset speaker with Lapid; Liberman indicated he would support replacing the speaker before pursuing coalition negotiations.
Related ToI liveblog snippets (2 Nov): Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu and his party of a "destructive and violent campaign of delegitimization against the election results." Eisenkot says these efforts are "a direct assault on Israeli democracy" and proof of the "grave danger posed by the continued rule of Likud and Netanyahu." Likud responds by claiming that Eisenkot is trying to stop "the truth from coming to light regarding the grave suspicions…concerning the contamination of the Israeli election by foreign elements."
